The code is unchanged from 93d1090, and 93d1090 was built against a document that did not contain requirement 3. SCOPE LIMIT, UNCHANGED I do not verify that any of this is announced. Everything below is attribute correctness, ID resolution and reference topology in the markup. Audibility is gate 3, Chang's. Nothing here is evidence about how any of it sounds. =================================================================== THE BLOCKING FINDING â€” REQUIREMENT 3 =================================================================== **One error element. Four references to it. Up to four of them live at once.** components/IntakeFlow.tsx: - 723: `const dutyToAccommodateErrorId = useId();` â€” called ONCE in StepNarrative. There is exactly one duty error id in the entire component. - 812-819: exactly one `

`, rendered as a SIBLING after all four fieldsets. It is not a descendant of any group. - 775, 786, 798, 808: all four RadioQuestion call sites pass that same single id as `describedById`, each gated on its own `xInvalid` flag. The gate-1 criterion in this sprint reads, verbatim: "QA1 confirms each group's `aria-describedby` resolves only to elements belonging to that group, and that no error-text element is referenced by more than one group." Whenever two or more duty questions are blank, two or more `xInvalid` flags are true simultaneously, and that one `role="alert"` element is referenced by two, three, or four groups at once. The criterion is not met. Requirement 3's first clause â€” "Error text is scoped per group" â€” is not met either: the text is scoped per *form*. It is a single summary string built at line 253 as `Missing: ${missingDutyToAccommodate.join(", ")}.`, so a user in the "alternatives considered" group is pointed at text that also names documentation timing and written record. THIS IS NOT AN EDGE CASE. It is the default path. Submit the duty section with nothing answered and every visible group is blank, every flag is true, and every group points at the same element. Sprint 9's own round-3 Dev Notes documented exactly this behaviour approvingly ("the three invalid groups still share one summary message naming all three"), which is fair evidence that nobody thinks it is a bug â€” under Sprint 9's requirements it was not one. Under this document it is. WHAT 93d1090 ACTUALLY FIXED, PRECISELY. It changed each call site's gate from the global `dutyToAccommodateError` to that question's own `xInvalid` flag. That fixes requirement 3's SECOND clause â€” "reaches no group that did not fail" â€” completely and correctly. A correctly-answered group now carries no error reference at all. It does nothing about the FIRST clause, because it did not change what the reference points AT. One shared id in, one shared id out. Requirement 3 states the two clauses as a matched pair and this file's Risks section names the exact failure mode: "Requirements 1 and 3 are treated as separable and one ships without the other." Half of requirement 3 is shipped. I want to be straight about my own position here, because I am the reason this needs saying. My out-of-band review of 93d1090 under Sprint 9 called the shared summary "one thing for gate 3 to listen for, not a defect," and said a per-field message "would be a new requirement, not an in-flight substitution." That was correct against Sprint 9's requirements. Master Controller has now written that requirement. The code did not change; the standard did. Passing this on the strength of my own prior review is precisely the risk this file predicted of me, and the answer to a new requirement being unmet is not that I already blessed the old code. =================================================================== ISSUE 2 â€” THE REQUIREMENT-4 DELIVERABLE CONTAINS A FALSE STATEMENT =================================================================== Sprint file line 267-268, Sprint 8 round 5 bullet, verbatim: "`describedBy` now composes only the current question's own error id (gated on that question's own `invalid` flag), not a globally-shared one." There is no per-question error id. `useId()` is called once at 723 and `dutyToAccommodateErrorId` is the only duty error id that exists; all four call sites pass that same value. The id IS globally shared â€” it is conditionally *referenced*, which is a different property. The sentence describes an implementation that is not in the file. This is not a wording quibble, and it is the reason I am flagging it at HIGH rather than filing it with the documentation notes. Requirement 4 makes this analysis an audited written deliverable, and this specific sentence is the one that makes requirement 3 look satisfied. An auditor reading Dev Notes and not the source would conclude per-group scoping had been implemented. The parenthetical "(gated on that question's own invalid flag)" is accurate and is doing the work of making the surrounding false claim sound checked. The honest version of that bullet is: the gating moved to per-question, the referenced element did not, and per-group error text remains unbuilt. =================================================================== ISSUE 3 â€” THE SELF-VERIFICATION TESTS THE ONE CASE THAT CANNOT FAIL =================================================================== Dev Notes' live check answers three questions and leaves exactly one blank (`writtenRecord`). With a single group failing, one group references the error element, so "no error-text element is referenced by more than one group" holds trivially. The scenario chosen is the only configuration of this form in which the new criterion cannot be violated. The conclusion drawn from it â€” "Zero correctly-answered groups resolve to any error element" â€” is true, and it establishes requirement 3's second clause. It is silent on the first, and the write-up presents it as "requirement 3's exact bar." Sprint 9 round 3's notes, on the same code, did test three-blank. The multi-missing case was checked once, under the prior sprint, and its result is the finding above. =================================================================== EVERYTHING ELSE â€” PASS =================================================================== REQUIREMENT 5, DIFF SCOPE â€” PASS. ` renders under the same test. `xInvalid` is `dutyToAccommodateError !== null && x === null`, so any true flag implies `dutyToAccommodateError` is non-null, which is what renders the error `

`. No dangling reference is reachable. The `!== null` versus truthiness asymmetry I recorded against 93d1090 remains unreachable, because the setter only ever receives `null` or a non-empty `Missing: â€¦` string. REQUIREMENT 4 COVERAGE â€” PASS as to presence, one bullet false as to content. All five prior rounds are named and analysed: Sprint 8 rounds 3, 4 and 5, and Sprint 9's naming fix and finding-4 fix. What it takes, so nobody has to guess at scope: - Each group needs its own error-text element with its own id and its own text â€” the message for that question alone, e.g. "Missing: written record." on the written-record group. - Deriving that per-group text from state that already exists is presentational and stays inside requirement 5. `missingDutyToAccommodate` is already built from per-question checks at 245-251; the four `xInvalid` booleans already exist. What requirement 3 forbids is a *group's* `aria-describedby` pointing at it. Keep the summary as an unreferenced live region, and point each group at its own message. - Requirement 7 then applies for real. If the per-group message is produced by a named function rather than inline JSX, it is a decision and it needs Vitest coverage. Markup-only is unlikely to survive this change; do not reach for the "no new pure function" clause reflexively. - Fix the round-5 bullet (issue 2) to describe what the code does. - Re-verify with two or more groups blank, not one. The single-blank scenario cannot detect this class of defect and should not be the evidence offered again. One question that is genuinely Master Controller's, not mine and not Dev Team's: if requirement 3 was intended to permit a shared summary across groups that actually failed, and to forbid only the leak onto correct groups, then this code satisfies the intent and the gate-1 criterion is written too tightly. That is an amendment for Master Controller to make explicitly, in the sprint file, before a re-audit. Scope discipline is exact, Sprint 9's naming work is intact, the corrected calibration attribution carried over properly, and the finding-4 fix is correct and correctly described. This sprint is one unbuilt requirement and one false sentence away from being auditable as a whole.
